content: UNASYN sterile powder is intended for intravenous (IV) or intramuscular (IM) administration and must be reconstituted using one of the compatible diluents specified in the product insert. After reconstitution, the solution should be allowed to stand to let any foam dissipate, enabling a clear visual inspection to confirm complete dissolution of the powder. For IV use, the recommended concentration of UNASYN ranges from 3 to 45 mg/mL, which corresponds to 2 to 30 mg of ampicillin and 1 to 15 mg of sulbactam per milliliter. When reconstituting the 15-gram vial, you may use either 92 mL of Sterile Water for Injection or 0.9% Sodium Chloride Injection as the diluent. The diluent should be added in two separate portions in a controlled environment, such as a laminar flow hood. First, add 50 mL of the diluent and shake the vial to dissolve the powder. Then, add the remaining 42 mL of diluent and shake again. Allow the solution to stand after mixing to let any foam dissipate, ensuring the solution is fully dissolved and clear. The final reconstituted solution will have a concentration of approximately 100 mg/mL of ampicillin and 50 mg/mL of sulbactam. After reconstitution, the solution must be used within two hours if stored at room temperature or within four hours if refrigerated. If the reconstituted bulk solution is stored at room temperature (20°C/68°F) for less than one hour before further dilution, the storage and usage times for the diluted solution are outlined in Table 6 of the product insert. If the bulk solution is stored at room temperature for one to two hours before dilution, the usage times specified in Table 7 apply, depending on the final concentration and diluent used. Any remaining solution that is not used within the specified time frames must be discarded. It is important to note that reversible glycogenosis was observed in laboratory animals during preclinical studies. However, this effect was both doseand time-dependent and is not anticipated to occur in humans when the drug is administered at therapeutic doses and plasma levels during the relatively short duration of combined ampicillin/sulbactam therapy.
